chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, judged regarding your blood (lives) with a ruling different from what He judged regarding your wealth. He judged regarding your wealth that the burden of proof is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the defendant; and He judged regarding your blood that the burden of proof is upon the one against whom it is claimed and the oath is upon the one who claims, so that the blood of a Muslim is not lost.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in burden of proof between financial claims and blood claims in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the jurisprudential principle of 'al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda'' (proof on the claimant) in financial matters versus 'al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda' lahu' (proof on the defendant) in blood disputes, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving life (nafs). The rationale provided—that this distinction prevents the nullification of a Muslim's blood—highs the gravity of homicide compared to property loss, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition and elaborated upon by scholars like al-Shaykh al-Mufid and al-Tusi in their discussions on qisas and diyah.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Judged with regards to your blood (lives) with other than what He<sup>azwj</sup> has Judged with regards to your wealth. 
A Judgement with regards to your wealth is that the burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the swearing is upon the defendant; and a Judgement with regards to your blood (life) is that the burden of proof is upon the defendant, but the swearing is upon the one who claims, so that the blood of a Muslim is not lost’.
